checked_classes: Ordering errors — verified the 34 tasks, the change-level dependency graph, the per-task predecessors, and the shared-file serialization rules (UAR host modules 01→04, UAR routes/actor/manager stay with 02, Boss bridge 02→04, Bossfang memory/task/dispatch one writer across 03's slices) align without deadlock; production can run in parallel where predecessors allow, V1/V2 deferred to completed boundaries per A-9; 04/5–6 P0 supplements are independent of 01–03 production and feed 04/7–8 P4R which then feed 04/9 V1, all consistent with the stop-conditions table

Missing dependencies — every goal bullet is covered by the 34 task contracts: F1/F5 in 03, F2/F3 in 01, F4 in 04, F6 in 02 (with 02/5 D0 prerequisite before 02/6 P2), F7 in 02, G7-A/B split across 01/04; retry/sweep/cron/restart in 03/6, auth.rs verified UserContext in 01/3–4, resource JWT/introspection in 04/1–4, stdio in 04/3, secret projection in 04/4, common vs receiver-specific split between 04/1–4 and 04/7–8

Untestable or ambiguous acceptance criteria — each gate section names a specific observable result (403/non-disclosing404, 409 admission_digest_conflict, exact approval ID, classification into acknowledgement/terminal/cleanup, dual remote/local evidence, etc.); the matrix explicitly rejects 'works correctly' phrasing and requires gate receipts to enumerate scenario pass/fail/blocked with source SHA, dirty diff digest, validator, backend, token class, isolated data namespace, sanitized request/result/effect count and limitations

Scope smuggling — every change's files in repository-bindings.json map to its assessment findings (F1–F7/G7-A/B); no bossfang/UAR/boss work added that the goals do not require; REMOTE claim correctly null with paths []; new proposed paths limited to additive modules (jwks_cache, secret_projection, harness_attempt, uar_harness/{mod,admission,observation,lifecycle}, tests/bauar_*) consistent with the 500-line rule and serial ownership transfers

Constraints compliance — A-1..A-17 respected: A-2 defensive code traces to named scenarios, A-3 security at real boundaries, A-4 minimal diff / no unrelated refactor, A-5 honest about unknowns (model identity, exact producer, RECOVERY-PROFILE-DECISION, ownership supplements), A-6 verification vs self-report, A-7 breaking changes called out per change, A-8 architecture before code, A-9 tests deferred to completed boundary with no unit-only/mock-only/old-binary closure, A-10 single-writer serialization for shared files, A-11 additive schema rollback, A-12 human approval at every stage, A-13 stop at plan completion, A-14 structured artifacts (plan.md, repository-bindings.json, evidence/), A-15 no Signed-off-by, A-16 F6 reproducer before report, A-17 plan mode default; §P: no new shell/python scripts, no new services, exactly two services respected, OpenSpec is spec backend, 500-line rule acknowledged in U-ID note, Node LTS only, no symlinks, no jq/grep/sed/awk/curl instruction

Spec warning integration — the spec review's auth.rs warning (verified UserContext at create/list/revoke, anonymous fallback removed, owner/tenant checks, non-disclosing denials, bounded exchange TTL, documented JWT revocation limit) is implemented in 01/3–4 contracts; the spec suggestion (separate allowed/disallowed/reserved-role fixtures) is adopted in 01/3 and the KEY acceptance section

Repository binding completeness — all 16 claim types defined, all paths present (existing + proposed-new) with explicit kind, owners are roles (not person names) with appropriate serialization notes (single writer for Bossfang memory/task/dispatch across 03 slices, transfer of host modules 01→04, transfer of Boss bridge 02→04, F-MCP and F-HARNESS need named claim record supplements), REMOTE intentionally unassigned per the stop conditions; 'no blanket API write grant' caveat for F-MCP and 'no backend wildcard is a write grant' for U-ID prevent silent expansion

Stop conditions and materialization — SOURCE-OWNERSHIP, C05-OWNERSHIP, ROOT-APPROVAL-COMPATIBILITY, F6-REPRODUCTION, RECOVERY-PROFILE-DECISION, REMOTE-RECEIVER-INVENTORY, REMOTE-RESOURCE-SECRET-STORE are all listed as blocking inputs with explicit dispatch-blocking scope; the plan is honest that these remain unresolved and does not pretend to answer them; no original C05 or shipping checkmark is changed; materialization requires explicit Execute handover

Per-task execution contracts — 34 task rows match the 34 task_baseline entries (7+8+9+10=34); predecessors and batch assignments are coherent with the dependency graph; claim sets (B-APPROVAL, U-TEST, F-HARNESS, etc.) match repository-bindings.json; each row's Additional binding / observable exit is specific (e.g. 'Require verified UserContext at create; allowed user, disallowed reader and reserved host-session/admin fixtures separately')

Task model assignments — 34 rows in the model assignments table, one per backend task, all using L1 launch contract with R1 model (gpt-6-astra/high) and R2 as alternative requiring explicit revision; R3 (MiniMax-M3) for L2 review only; model identity explicitly unverified, recheck at dispatch called out; provider role preserves Bossfang team's Claude opus role instructions and maps execution to gpt-6-astra/high; L2 is packet-only POST with reviewer mandate, no generation history or tool-execution claims

F6 handling — D0 diagnostic on unchanged baseline with real JWT middleware is a true prerequisite to any binding remediation; the plan correctly distinguishes diagnostic (02/5), conditional correction (02/6), and final V1 (02/7) and rejects non-run branch closure; 'no JWT-disabled fixture' rule is preserved; closure receipt must name the production module/function/code branch that compared authenticated owner with stored session owner, not JWT validity alone

Rollout and rollback — explicit that no rollout is published during Plan; rollback preserves receipts, pending decisions, unknown outcomes; never restores insecure remote validation, run-only approval fallback, plaintext custody, cross-owner pooling, or automatic replay; additive schema rollback retains records, destructive migration requires separate authorization; existing in-flight completion-driver work is not reclassified as full-harness admission
adaptation: Node24 LTS REST; packet only; vendor reasoning block discarded without persistence; no unsupported reasoning setting.
